articles.title: Diljit Dosanjh REFUSES to back out of Indore show on November 15 despite bomb threat emails and song restrictions: 'Do they know who are we?'
articles.summary: Diljit Dosanjh has made it clear that he will perform at his Indore concert on November 15, even though the show has run into security alarms and
articles.body: Diljit Dosanjh has made it clear that he will perform at his Indore concert on November 15, even though the show has run into security alarms and objections over his songs. The singer, who is bringing his AURA India Tour to the city, said he is determined to honour the promise he made to his fans.Diljit Dosanjh sends a message to his Indore fansSpeaking about the controversies, the Punjabi star said he would reach the city on the scheduled date. He also gave a light-hearted mention to Indore’s famous street food.According to the NDTV report, he said, "I will visit Indore on 15th of November. I will have poha first after visiting Indore. Anyone can say anything, but I will meet you in Indore on 15th November. I have heard in the news that there will be some ‘sankat’. But we know how to handle this. Do they know who are we?"His comments come at a time when there is plenty of uncertainty around the show. Over the past few days, the concert has been linked with bomb threats, safety worries and an order to drop some songs from the setlist.Bomb threat emails create tension in IndoreEarlier this week, three private schools and the office of Indore Mayor Pushyamitra Bhargava got emails threatening a bomb blast on the day of the concert. The emails also advised schools not to send their students to the event.Bomb disposal teams checked all three school campuses, but no explosive material was found. Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Rajesh Dandotiya said early findings indicated that the emails may be hoaxes. The crime branch is now studying technical evidence to trace who sent them.Four songs under the scannerThe threats were not the only issue. On November 6, the District Child Protection Officer in Indore asked the management of C-21 Mall, the venue, to make sure Diljit does not perform four songs. These are ‘Patiala Pegg’, ‘5 Taara Theeke’, ‘Jeeb Vicho Labbiya’ and ‘Jatt Uthe Fire Karda Jithe Pabandi Hathiyara Di’.The direction came after a complaint by Chandigarh-based professor Dr Panditrao Dharennavar, who objected to lyrics that, according to him, promote liquor, drugs and weapons. The official letter also cited a 2019 order of the Punjab and Haryana High Court on songs that glorify intoxicants and violence. The venue has been told to follow these instructions.Not the first time Diljit has faced hurdlesThe situation in Indore is not new for the singer, who has had to deal with obstacles in other cities as well. His October 30 concert at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Delhi was also in doubt after the Delhi Police first held back permission. The reasons given were security concerns and law-and-order arrangements during the festive period.The organisers then gave the police an updated security plan with extra steps for safety, traffic and crowd control. Once permission came through, the show went on as planned. Reports suggest around 2,000 security personnel were deployed, and a 700-metre no-car zone was set up around the venue.After the Delhi show, Diljit said some people had made strong attempts to stop the concert. He also thanked the police personnel who helped make sure it took place.Bihar plans fall throughIn a recent Instagram Live, the singer revealed that his plan to perform in Bihar did not work out. The reason was a disagreement over who would be responsible for managing the crowd. As per Diljit, officials expected him to handle the audience, while he felt this was a job for the administration.Recalling the talks, he said that controlling the crowd at a concert is a big task that needs a lot of planning on the ground. He compared it to arranging a huge event in Delhi.Where will Diljit Dosanjh perform next?The Indore show is part of the ongoing AURA India Tour 2026. The Indian leg began with the Delhi concert, and Indore is next on November 15. After that, the singer will perform in Ahmedabad on November 21, Mumbai on November 27, Bengaluru on November 29, Lucknow on December 5, Chandigarh on December 12 and Kolkata on December 19.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Salman Khan lauds Chitrangada Singh’s confidence, says, 'There is a punch in chemistry'
articles.summary: Salman Khan is gearing up for the release of his upcoming film, 'Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace', which also features Chitrangada Singh in a key role.
articles.body: Salman Khan is gearing up for the release of his upcoming film, 'Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace', which also features Chitrangada Singh in a key role. At the film's trailer launch, when asked what makes his co-star stand out, the actor praised her confidence and said she never allows insecurities to affect her.At the event, a journalist asked Salman, “Aishwarya Rai, then Katrina Kaif and now Chitrangada Singh. So, you gave a kick which injured her. But tell us a little about your chemistry and explain her qualities.”Salman responded in his trademark witty style, saying, “There is a punch in chemistry.” When asked about Chitrangada's best quality, he added, “No insecurity at all.”Salman Khan and Chitrangada Singh’s first film together'Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace' marks the first on-screen collaboration between Salman Khan and Chitrangada Singh. The film is inspired by the 2020 Galwan Valley clashes between Indian and Chinese troops and draws on accounts from Shiv Aroor's book, 'India’s Most Fearless'.Directed by Apoorva Lakhia, the film features Salman as Indian Army Colonel Bikkumalla Santosh Babu, who commanded the 16 Bihar Regiment during the Galwan Valley clash and was posthumously awarded the Maha Vir Chakra. The supporting cast includes Mukesh Rishi, Ankur Bhatia, Zeyn Shaw and Abhilash Chaudhary.'Maatrubhumi' release dateInitially announced as 'Battle of Galwan', the film was later renamed 'Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace'. Salman revealed that the release was delayed because the team needed additional time to perfect the VFX and meet its visual standards. The production schedule also needed adjustments following Chitrangada Singh's injury. The film is now scheduled to hit theatres on December 4.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Surekha Vani says Instagram account was hacked, warns of legal action over sharing private content
articles.summary: Actress Surekha Vani has spoken out about the circulation of her private content, claiming that her Instagram account was hacked.
articles.body: Actress Surekha Vani has spoken out about the circulation of her private content, claiming that her Instagram account was hacked. The Telugu actress has urged social media users, meme pages and media platforms not to share or repost the content without her permission. She has also issued a strong warning against using the incident to gain views, increase online reach or generate publicity. Her statement has once again drawn attention to concerns surrounding online privacy and the misuse of personal content involving celebrities.Taking to Instagram, Surekha Vani said that her private content had been circulated without her consent following the alleged hacking of her account. She directly appealed to meme pages, media platforms, YouTube channels and individuals to stop uploading or circulating the material in any form.The actress also made it clear that she would take legal action against anyone found sharing or publishing her private content. In her statement, she said, "Any account or person found sharing, publishing, or further spreading my private content will be identified, documented, and legal action will be taken against them."She stressed that the matter was serious and should not be treated as an opportunity to generate online engagement.Actress says incident should not be used for publicitySurekha Vani further urged social media users not to exploit the situation to gain popularity or increase their online reach. She asked everyone to respect her privacy and refrain from spreading the content any further.The actress reiterated that she would consider legal action against those who ignored her appeal. Her statement comes amid discussions about the circulation of alleged personal videos on social media. She has made it clear that sharing such material without consent is unacceptable and that those responsible could face legal consequences.Surekha Vani remains active on social mediaSurekha Vani has appeared in several Telugu films, often portraying mothers, sisters and other family-oriented characters. While she has continued to work in films, the actress also remains active on social media, where she regularly shares pictures and videos.Her daughter, Supritha, has also been gaining popularity among audiences through her presence in the entertainment industry and on digital platforms. The mother-daughter duo often shares pictures and reels on their respective social media accounts.However, with the latest incident, Surekha Vani has made a strong appeal for people to respect her privacy and refrain from circulating personal content without consent.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: In 1980, Stephen King bought a $135,000 Victorian mansion in Maine; today, it preserves his literary archives and supports writers with $2,500 grants
articles.summary: Stephen King’s association with Bangor, Maine, goes beyond the fictional horror stories that have made him one of the world’s best-known authors.
articles.body: Stephen King’s association with Bangor, Maine, goes beyond the fictional horror stories that have made him one of the world’s best-known authors. A striking Victorian property that he and his wife, Tabitha King, purchased in 1980 has since taken on a different purpose. The former family home is now intended to preserve the author’s literary legacy, while a neighbouring historic mansion provides a place for selected writers to work on their projects.The couple bought the property at 47 West Broadway for $135,000. Its distinctive red exterior and elaborate black wrought-iron entrance gate, featuring bats, spiders and other Gothic details, have made it one of Bangor’s most recognisable houses. The property also has a connection to the city that influenced the setting of King’s 1986 horror novel It.Stephen King’s former home is now a centre for literary preservationKing and Tabitha spent several decades associated with the Bangor residence, where they raised their family. However, the couple eventually decided that the property could serve a wider purpose than remaining a private home.In 2019, the Bangor City Council approved their proposal to convert the property into a nonprofit centre. The plan included moving King’s extensive collection of literary material to the residence. The archive contains manuscripts, photographs, personal notes, articles, audio recordings, videos and other documents connected to his writing career.The collection offers researchers and scholars an opportunity to explore the work and creative history of the bestselling author. Access to the archive is available by appointment rather than through regular public tours.Brown Mansion offers writers a 10-day residency and $2,500Another important part of the project is located next door. The historic Brown Mansion has been developed into a writers’ retreat under the Stephen and Tabitha King Foundation.The programme invites selected writers to spend 10 days at the property, giving them an opportunity to concentrate on their creative projects away from their usual routines. Participants receive private bedrooms and bathrooms, shared living spaces, access to a stocked kitchen and nightly dinners during their stay.The foundation also provides each selected writer with a $2,500 honorarium. The amount can be used towards travel expenses or other personal requirements, allowing participants to make the most of their residency.The retreat is designed to bring together small groups of writers, offering them both privacy and opportunities to interact with other creative professionals. Its location also gives residents access to Bangor’s local community.A property that connects Stephen King’s legacy with emerging writersThe transformation of the two properties reflects a broader effort by Stephen and Tabitha King to support literature and preserve the author’s work. Instead of turning the famous residence into a conventional tourist attraction, the couple chose to give it a role centred on research, writing and literary preservation.The archive safeguards material from King’s decades-long career, while the neighbouring retreat provides financial assistance and dedicated working space to writers selected for the programme.What began as a $135,000 property purchase in 1980 has therefore developed into a literary project with two distinct purposes: preserving the work of an established author and creating opportunities for other writers to develop their own.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Chainsaw robot looks terrifying but has a real job
articles.summary: JR East's towering ZIZAI ZX-3 chainsaw robot tackles dangerous branch-cutting along Japan's Koumi Line while a trained operator controls it remotely.
articles.body: If you saw a humanoid robot holding a chainsaw next to train tracks, you'd probably do a double take. I know I would. But that's exactly what's happening in Japan, where a towering chainsaw robot is cutting back branches that could interfere with passing trains. It's a little intimidating to watch, especially when you see how high this machine can reach. Still, there's a pretty good reason railway crews are putting it to work. Japan's JR East railway company is using the chainsaw robot to handle dangerous maintenance jobs that would normally require workers to operate heavy cutting equipment high above the ground. The robot does the physical work while a person controls its movements from a safer location. I find that reassuring, especially when a chainsaw is involved. So how does this unusual machine actually work, and could it change the way dangerous maintenance jobs get done? Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover five ways to travel smarter and save money. Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed. Watch the free replay and downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com. HUMANOID ROBOTS PERFORM LIVE SURGERY IN WORLD FIRST How the chainsaw robot clears railway tracks The robot has been put to work along JR East's Koumi Line in central Japan, where overgrown branches can create problems for passing trains. What's interesting is how the machine actually handles the cutting. One mechanical arm grips a branch while the other operates the chainsaw. The robot's upper body extends from a boom mounted on a specialized maintenance vehicle, allowing it to reach high above the tracks. That means workers can tackle branches that would normally require someone to operate cutting equipment at height. The robot even has a name, ZIZAI ZX-3. Japanese manufacturer Nippon Signal announced its delivery to JR East earlier this year. The machine began full-scale maintenance work along the Koumi Line in October. And this technology already has some experience behind it. JR West started using a related robotic system in July 2024. What's especially appealing about this approach is that the machine takes on the dangerous physical work while a trained operator stays at a safer distance. Who's actually controlling this chainsaw robot? Now, before you start worrying about robots running around with chainsaws, the ZX-3 is actually controlled by a person. A trained operator guides the robot remotely, deciding where to position its arms and when to start cutting. That's important because working near railway tracks requires careful attention. One wrong move could damage equipment or put someone in danger. So while the robot handles the heavy lifting, a human still makes the decisions. Nippon Signal designed the ZX-3 to make it easier for workers to control the robot's movements. Right now, its main job is cutting back trees and branches that grow too close to railway lines. However, the company hopes to give it additional tools so it can handle other maintenance work in the future. And here's what I find interesting. Workers still need the skills to do the job, but now they can operate the equipment from a safer location. That's a pretty big change when you're talking about working high above train tracks with a chainsaw. Why railway companies are turning to robots Keeping train tracks clear takes more work than you might realize. Branches can grow close enough to interfere with passing trains, and cutting them back sometimes means sending workers high above the tracks with heavy equipment. That brings some serious safety risks, especially when crews are working near electrical infrastructure. Japan is also dealing with a shortage of skilled workers, so JR East is looking for ways to make these jobs safer and less physically demanding. That's where the chainsaw robot comes in. It can reach areas that would be difficult or dangerous for workers to access while the operator stays at a safer distance. JR East is also changing when some of this work gets done. Since 2022, the company has been moving certain maintenance jobs along the Koumi Line into daytime hours instead of having crews work overnight. That sometimes means temporarily canceling trains, which I'm sure passengers aren't thrilled about. But it also gives workers better conditions and more manageable schedules. And when you combine that with a robot that can handle dangerous cutting work, you can see why JR East is investing in this technology. NEW AI BRAIN LETS ROBOTS MOVE LIKE HUMANS Could AI eventually control a robot with a chainsaw? Now this is where I start having a few more questions. JR East has been investing in artificial intelligence and robotics across its railway operations. The company is exploring ways to use AI for equipment inspections and other maintenance activities. Its broader technology plans include robots that can help inspect infrastructure. That raises an interesting possibility. Could a future version of this chainsaw robot identify an overgrown branch and cut it without someone guiding every movement? It's certainly a direction robotics developers could explore. AI-powered image analysis could help identify vegetation that threatens railway operations. More advanced systems might eventually assist with some of the decisions an operator makes today. But there's an important difference between what might be possible and what JR East has actually announced. The ZX-3 currently relies on human control, and JR East has not announced a timeline for making its chainsaw operation fully autonomous. Personally, I think that's worth emphasizing. Giving a robot greater independence sounds impressive until you consider what happens if it misidentifies an object or someone enters its working area. We recently covered how humanoid robots are getting new workplace safety systems. Those safeguards will become even more important as machines take on jobs involving powerful tools. What this means to you You may never see this particular chainsaw robot working near your local train station. However, the technology behind it could eventually change how infrastructure gets maintained closer to home. If you ride commuter trains, you already know how frustrating delays can be. Overgrown vegetation can contribute to service disruptions, and railway companies spend considerable time keeping tracks clear. Equipment that helps crews perform those jobs safely and efficiently could eventually benefit passengers. There are potential applications beyond railways, too. Utility companies regularly need to trim vegetation around power lines. Construction crews also handle dangerous work in areas that are difficult to reach. Remotely operated machines could help reduce some of those risks. Of course, there's another side to this. As robots become more capable, companies will need workers who know how to operate and maintain them. That could create opportunities for new skills while changing the way traditional maintenance jobs are performed. And while robots can reduce certain dangers, they bring their own safety concerns. A machine handling a chainsaw still needs reliable controls and proper oversight. For now, the ZX-3 shows how robotics can help people perform hazardous work without placing them directly in the path of danger. ONE OF THE WORLD'S HOTTEST INDUSTRIES IS SPARKING A BLUE-COLLAR JOBS BOOM Kurt's key takeaways I've seen plenty of humanoid robots doing backflips and showing off what they can do. But there's something different about watching one actually earn its keep. Seeing this robot handle a chainsaw high above the tracks makes me think about the risks workers face doing that job themselves. And if it can help keep railway workers out of dangerous situations, I am all for it. What I especially like is that there's still a person making the decisions. The operator brings the experience while the machine takes on the physically demanding work. That seems like a sensible way to introduce robotics into jobs where mistakes can have serious consequences. What I'll be watching is how quickly companies push these machines toward greater independence. AI is advancing, and I suspect we'll see more robots taking on jobs that once seemed impossible to automate. But when the tool in a robot's hand is a chainsaw, I want to know someone is paying very close attention. Would you trust a fully autonomous robot to operate a chainsaw near the trains you ride? articles.title: La premonición de Grison sobre los invitados de 'La Revuelta' que se vuelve viral en redes: “Abascal no creo que venga en la pu** vida”
articles.standfirst: El colaborador habló sobre los posibles invitados del programa durante su participación en el pódcast 'Tómatelo con vino'
articles.summary: El colaborador habló sobre los posibles invitados del programa durante su participación en el pódcast 'Tómatelo con vino'
articles.body: Grison ha protagonizado un momento que no ha tardado en circular por las redes sociales tras hablar sobre los posibles invitados de 'La Revuelta'. El colaborador de David Broncano participó en el pódcast 'Tómatelo con vino', donde le preguntaron si el programa tenía vetado a algún personaje público. Su respuesta terminó poniendo sobre la mesa los nombres de Santiago Abascal y Pedro Sánchez. Todo comenzó cuando le plantearon directamente: “¿Tenéis vetado a alguien en el programa?”. Grison respondió inicialmente con dudas, pero pronto lanzó una predicción sobre el líder de Vox: “Yo creo que a Abascal no va a venir en la p*** vida. Las cosas como son”. A continuación, mencionó también a Vito Quiles, aunque dejó abierta la posibilidad de que pudieran llamarlos en algún momento. La conversación fue más allá cuando surgió la posibilidad de recibir a Abascal en el sofá del podcast. Una de las participantes defendió que el equipo tendría que estar preparado para entrevistar a cualquier político, “da igual de qué partido sea”. En ese momento, se introdujo una comparación con el presidente del Gobierno y las presentadoras de' Tómatelo con vino' respondieron lo siguiente :”Nosotros tenemos vetado aquí a Pedro Sánchez”. Al preguntarle si era el único nombre de la lista, respondió afirmativamente, lo que provocó una nueva reacción. Grison, respondió: “Pero si metéis a Abascal, meted a Pedro Sánchez”. La respuesta fue contundente: “No, porque uno está gobernando y haciéndolo mal y el otro no”. La conversación continuó con una pregunta directa sobre si no querían recibir a Sánchez, a lo que Grison contestó: “No”. El intercambio terminó entre bromas y comentarios sobre si alguno de los invitados había podido llevarse algo del camerino. El fragmento ha generado comentarios en redes por las declaraciones del colaborador y su pronóstico sobre una posible visita de Abascal a 'La Revuelta'.
